summary: Camille Bulcke was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at KU Leuven, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. From 1949 to 1957, he served as Head of the Sanskrit and Hindi Department at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai.

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Milan and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. His career includes posts at Cambridge, Würzburg, Oxford, and the Bodleian Library.

Canan Yoğurt is an Indologist who studied at Ankara University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She held posts as a research assistant at Erciyes University (2014–2024), a researcher at the University of Hyderabad (2017), and a researcher in Indology at Çukurova University (2024).
Carel Gabriel Cobet was a linguistics scholar who studied at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University. He served on the faculty at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.
Carl A. P. Ruck is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965). He held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Arendt was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Heymann Steinthal (1856–1859). From 1887 to 1902, he was a teacher (Lehrer) at the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Carl Bezold was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Friedrich Delitzsch. In 1886, he founded the Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und Vorderasiatische Archäologie, and he held a post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1894 to 1922.

Carl Bielefeldt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and at UC Berkeley. He served on the editorial board and as an emeritus professor at Stanford University, and belonged to the Numata Center.

Carl Brockelmann was a linguist and historian who studied at Rostock, Breslau, and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. He held academic posts at Breslau, Humboldt University, Königsberg, Halle-Wittenberg, and Frederick William University Berlin.

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber in Berlin, as well as at Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from 1875 to 1921.

Carl Christian Rafn was a Danish scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from approximately 1814 to 1816 and held a post there from around 1821 to 1823.

Carl Darling Buck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale, the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, and Leipzig under William Dwight Whitney, Karl Brugmann, and August Leskien. He was a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

Carl Ferdinand Friedrich Lehmann-Haupt was a historian and archaeologist. Over his career, he held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1910), the University of Greifswald (~1914–1915), Istanbul University (~1915–1918), and the University of Innsbruck (~1918–1932).

Carl Fredrik Bergstedt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Otto Fredrik Tullberg. He also studied under Christian Lassen, Eugène Burnouf, and Niels Ludvig Westergaard between 1845 and 1848.

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, the University of Göttingen under Georg Christoph Lichtenberg and Christian Gottlob Heyne, and the University of Helmstedt. From 1807 to 1855, he was a full professor at Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.

Carl Friedrich Lottner was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1851–1854). He served as Lecturer (1860) and Professor of Sanskrit (1864) at Trinity College, Hartford.
Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena by 1877 under Berthold Delbrück, and also studied under Eduard Sievers and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung was a scholar of religious studies and medicine who completed his medical degree at the University of Basel. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Gustav Ruben Diehl was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his undergraduate and doctoral degrees at Lund University. He subsequently held docent positions at Lund University (1954–1959) and Uppsala University (1960–1966).

Carl Hjalmar Borgstrøm was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Oslo. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, Ankara University, Lund University, and served as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1947 to 1976.
